markingPoints.description: The conservation projects are now focusing on biodiversity
The focus is on biodiversity rather than on a few of its components
The whole range of life is taken into account, not only single components

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: The conservation projects are now focusing on biodiversity. Step 2: They are focusing on biodiversity rather than on a few of its components. Step 3: The whole range of life is therefore taken into account, and not only single well-known species. Step 4: Increasingly, even insects are beginning to find a place in conservation planning. Step 5: Insects are now counted in conservation work alongside the larger and better-known species.

A forest surveyor has been asked to prepare a note on the forest land that cannot be used up casually. She observes that in her work reserved forests and protected forests are treated together, and that together they go by another name. She records that these lands are kept for more than one purpose: one has to do with what the forest yields, and the other has to do with safeguarding the forest itself. She notes that a single state, Madhya Pradesh, has the largest area of such land, accounting for 75 per cent of its total forest area.

(a) What two categories of forest land together go to make up permanent forest estates? (b) Name the two purposes for which permanent forest estates are maintained. (c) A student says permanent forest estates exist only so that timber can be cut; use the two purposes to show why this is only half the case.

questions.stem:
A wildlife officer is revising the list of species that may not be harmed. She notes that conservation projects are now focusing on one thing rather than on a few of its components, and that this has brought a more intensive search for different conservation measures. She also records that, in the notification under the Wildlife Act of 1980 and 1986, several hundred butterflies, moths, beetles and one dragonfly were added to the list of protected species. She remarks that a list holding hundreds of butterfly, moth and beetle kinds but only a single dragonfly is far wider than any list of a few famous animals.

(a) What are conservation projects now focusing on, and what are they no longer focusing on? (b) Three kinds of insect and one dragonfly were added to the list of protected species under a notification; name two of the insect kinds. (c) Explain what a list made up of hundreds of butterfly, moth and beetle kinds and only one dragonfly tells a reader about the range of life that conservation work now covers.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
A reporter visits a Himalayan area where villagers have taken forests into their own hands, and also a set of villages where local people are conserving their traditional habitats along with government officials. In the Himalayan area the reporter learns that a famous movement has not only successfully resisted deforestation in several areas but has also shown that community afforestation with indigenous species can be enormously successful. Elsewhere, the communities are struggling to conserve their habitats along with government officials, recognising that only this will secure their forest and wildlife resources.

(a) Name the famous movement in the Himalayas that has successfully resisted deforestation in several areas. (b) Local communities in some areas are conserving their habitats along with government officials; what do they now recognise will secure their forest and wildlife resources? (c) A reader who credits only government departments for forest protection is missing part of the story; explain why the Himalayan movement and the recognition made by the villages both show that community effort matters.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) The Chipko movement. (b) Only this - the community's own conservation effort. (c) Because efforts such as the Chipko movement have themselves successfully resisted deforestation in several areas, and the communities recognise that only their own effort will secure their forest and wildlife resources.
